hints.junior: The error said 'Target closed' and nothing else — no screenshot, no idea what the page looked like when it failed.
hints.mid: One log line is consistent with a crash, a redirect, an overlay stealing the click, or a slow render — four causes, one indistinguishable message.
hints.staff: A suite with no failure artifacts isn't missing debugging info by accident — that's exactly what you configured it to keep, which by default is stdout only.

hints.junior: Click through both modes on the same failed test and see how much you can actually figure out in each one.
hints.mid: Broken mode gives you the log line and nothing else. Fixed mode gives you the DOM snapshot, screenshot, and network entry at the point of failure.
hints.staff: The overlay element that actually caused the failure only ever shows up in the DOM snapshot — it was never in the error message at all.

hints.junior: trace: 'on-first-retry' (or 'retain-on-failure') saves a trace.zip for any failing test — open it in the Trace Viewer for a full timeline.
hints.mid: on-first-retry only records on a retry, so passing tests cost nothing; retain-on-failure records every test but keeps only the failures.
hints.staff: Traces reconstruct the real DOM and accessibility tree per action, plus expect diffs and source-mapped stack frames — not a pixel video, an inspectable state machine.

hints.junior: The trace.zip has to actually leave the CI runner — upload it as a build artifact and link it from the failed job, or nobody finds it.
hints.mid: on-first-retry needs retries: 1 or higher configured to ever fire — a common gotcha is turning on tracing and seeing zero traces because retries are still 0.
hints.staff: Set a retention window for trace storage, and consider trace: 'on' scoped to one file while actively de-flaking a borderline test, not just the ones that hard-fail.

sections.junior: So a checkout test failed overnight in CI, and the only thing anyone had to go on was one line: target closed. No screenshot, no idea what the page even looked like.
sections.mid: That one log line is equally consistent with a crash, a redirect, or an overlay stealing the click — you genuinely cannot tell which from the text alone.
sections.staff: This is exactly why flaky failures cost so much more than their frequency suggests — every one turns into a re-run-and-guess cycle instead of an actual diagnosis.

sections.junior: Playwright can record a full trace for a test — turn it on with trace colon on-first-retry, and any failing test saves a timeline you can actually open and scrub through.
sections.mid: On first retry only records when a test gets retried after failing, so it costs nothing on the tests that pass, and you get a real DOM reconstruction, not a screen recording.
sections.staff: The trace captures the accessibility tree at each step, plus assertion diffs and source-mapped stack frames, so a failure buried in a page object still points at a specific line.

sections.junior: Try both modes here on the same failed test and see how much you can actually work out from each one.
sections.mid: The broken mode is the log line alone. The fixed mode shows you the DOM snapshot, the screenshot, and the network call at the exact moment things went wrong.
sections.staff: Watch for the overlay element in the fixed mode — that's the real root cause, and it was never mentioned anywhere in the original error text.

sections.junior: A bare error tells you where the test gave up, not what the page looked like. Turn tracing on so next time you get a real timeline instead of a guess.
sections.mid: Trace on first retry, or retain on failure if you're not using retries — either way you get a full DOM, network, and console timeline for the cost of a CI artifact upload.
sections.staff: DOM snapshots close a gap video can't — they show you the actual overlay or timing race, not just pixels. Budget the storage and wire up the CI upload, or the capability sits unused.
